content:
Nuevo Laredo marked 60 years of Plan DN-III-E, the Mexican Army and Air Force disaster-response mechanism that steps in to help civilians when natural disasters and other emergencies overwhelm local capacity, according to El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo. The plan's legal basis dates to 1965, and its first deployment came on October 10, 1966, after the Pánuco River overflowed along the Veracruz–Tamaulipas border.

Sgt. First Class of War Materials José Rubén Bustillos Varela explained that activation is not tied to a preset risk level but to need at the moment — above all when an emergency exceeds what local governments can handle. The work can include evacuations, temporary shelters, community kitchens and other support, the report says.

In Nuevo Laredo, the plan has been used after the storms of May 21, 2017, the downpour of May 21, 2020, and the severe storm of May 17, 2021, which damaged infrastructure, roads and basic services, according to El Mañana. Military personnel also supported logistics and vaccination during the COVID-19 emergency. Because of the city's geography, most local deployments have involved flooding, though the plan covers different kinds of natural disasters. This year it was activated for rain, mainly to help evacuate people, and no shelters were needed because the damage was minor. About 600 military personnel are available in Nuevo Laredo to join relief work as needed, the report says.

Sources:

  • El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo, "Plan DN-III-E cumple 60 años y en Nuevo Laredo destacan su importancia," October 31, 2026

title: Nuevo Laredo marks 60 years of Plan DN-III-E, the Army's disaster-response lifeline
